watchme.trigger: every entry through chart.live's one door — the drain runs there by design ('the read is the event — compile-on-read, never a clock, never a daemon'), so the probe rides the event the stone already chose rather than adding a second one.
watchme.enough: THREE CONSECUTIVE DRAINS THAT EMPTY THE LEDGER against real verdict artifacts, not fixtures. Three because the failure being watched was not intermittent — the drain failed at all seven following door entries on 2026-07-29 — so one success is indistinguishable from a small artifact getting lucky under the embed ceiling, and the ceiling is the actual suspect.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier (the default), plus the rendered CHAR LENGTH of each artifact attempted and whether the host accepted it. The length is not decoration: the measured boundary is 7403 accepted / 7447 refused against nomic-bert.context_length=2048, and the artifact that killed the crossing was 11283 chars. Without the length the probe can say 'it failed' and never say why.
watchme.nexus: chart's hypothesize tree — the same tree the drain feeds, so what killed the deposit lands in the memory of what-killed-which rather than beside it.
watchme.consumer: whoever next opens a deposit face in chart or librarian. Named that way on purpose: the ticket was kicked back because 'bounding a rendering against an embed context touches every deposit face in chart and librarian', so the reader who needs this is the one about to walk into the same wall.
watchme.authored: 2026-07-31 — SPEC ONLY, NOT A CROSSING. Recorded so the next pass does not re-derive it. The v1->v2 migration and the WATCHME crossing are a separate act through emit_migrated(workflow_str, target, watch='deposit-drain'), which is THE ONE DOOR for a migration crossing (it migrates and journals migrated_from together, so the record cannot lie). The chokepoint will refuse the crossing until the probe berth above exists and declares a module-level PROBE with both a carry and an enough — armed is MEASURED, not asserted.
watchme.probe_note: Berthed WITH what it watches — the drain lives in cairn/machines/chart/live.py — never beside this ticket, per the probe rule. NOT YET ARMED. (The prose that now lives in this field was originally written INTO `probe` on 2026-07-31 and armed_error() rejected the whole string as a path, which is the field doing its job: `probe` is consumed as a berth path, not as a description. Caught by running the validator instead of reading it.)
